# Independent origination, before literature/Astra retrieval

2026-11-01. Single Sol research worker; no delegated scientific work.

Selected consequential objective: acquire a finite, physically valid simulator for a bounded quantum system coupled to a genuinely gapless thermal continuum, with resource growth substantially slower than simulated time and with a certified system-channel error. Full success would provide a reusable primitive for reliable quantum materials/chemistry/open-system dynamics, rather than a finite diagnostic for one supplied fixture. This is an enabling-capability objective; a civilisation-changing outcome is not claimed.

Obstruction: continuum correlations decay algebraically, while finite positive Markovian auxiliary models typically have exponentially decaying correlations and eventually recur or produce the wrong low-frequency response. Pointwise correlation fitting can conceal accumulated channel error, wrong zero-temperature negative-frequency noise, or a hidden large Hilbert-space cutoff. One cannot assume a spectral gap, access to an exact simulator, or an already acquired bath decomposition.

Concrete initial attempt A: compress the accumulated influence functional (integrated correlation), using logarithmically separated time scales, into positive damped oscillator components. For an Ohmic zero-temperature test bath the integrated dephasing influence is logarithmic. Try to obtain logarithmic auxiliary count while retaining complete positivity and the bath thermal relation. Derive the exact large-time contribution of each positive damped mode before claiming an approximation. If the contribution is unavoidably linear, separate finite-horizon approximation from uniform-in-time simulation.

A different positive mechanism, if damped-mode compression fails, is an online unitary multiscale rotation of fresh bath modes, retaining only combinations with significant future coupling. This would compress physical quantum memory rather than use signed fitted noise. Its hard operation is earning causal low rank and a channel error under noncommuting system interactions. A pure-dephasing result alone does not establish that extension.
